A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same KCS research work. All 13 pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original knowledge-selection and downstream QA experiments, ablations and question-quality evaluations in Tables 1–4, plus the logical-coherence evaluation in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations and Appendix D's logical-coherence study.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix E retain the same sentence encoder, sentence-level Transformer, classification and contrastive objectives, nucleus sampling and MixQG question generation. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use HotpotQA and 2WikiMultihopQA for knowledge-composition selection and downstream multi-hop QA evaluation. The question-generation examples and logical-coherence scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same retrieval, classification, sentence-graph, LLM and random/MAX comparators. Tables 2–3 retain RAST, Composition and GPT-4; Table 2's original-data controls and Appendix D's ground-truth comparison are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same splits, filtering, metrics and model settings, including 5,000 original training examples for augmentation and 200 selected downstream test examples per LLM. Sampling settings remain Nq=5, K=3 and top-p=0.95; Appendix D's evaluation design also matches.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Table 4 retain identical architecture, sentence-order, composition-length, concatenation, hyperparameter and classification-integration ablations. The examples, case study and logical-coherence analysis in Appendices B–D are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither adds repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative examples match. For example, Table 1's KCS BERT-base F1@2/F1@3 remain 58.70/55.52 on HotpotQA and 78.39/72.75 on 2WikiMultihopQA; Table 6's KCS coherence scores remain 74.11 and 69.99.

T1.justification: The task definitions, probabilistic formulation, Equations (1)–(4) and top-p nucleus definition are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: diversifying knowledge compositions, sentence-level conditional prediction with contrastive learning, and stochastic decoding. The claimed 3.9% overall selection improvement and downstream augmentation benefits are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of knowledge coherence and diversity, attribution of inconsistent questions to the generation component, and discussion of human/LLM evaluation disagreements. The Limitations section preserves the same qualifications and future directions.

D1.justification: The preprocessing instructions, model choices, optimizers, learning rates, LoRA settings and sampling details are identical. The code and pretrained-model access links also retain the same targets.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged. Both position KCS against sentence classification, graph-based question generation and diversification methods operating on fixed knowledge compositions.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, dated 28 August 2025, to v2, dated 11 April 2026. The title, authors, prose, section order and appendices are otherwise unchanged; apparent spacing differences in extracted text are extraction artifacts.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7, Tables 1–6 and Algorithm 1 retain their displays, captions and placement. Visual inspection confirms the same page layout, table structures, plot axes and legends.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the same method, experimental evidence, mathematical exposition and limitations, including all appendix analyses. The updated arXiv version/date stamp and negligible rendering differences do not meaningfully change readability, reproducibility or scientific support.
